classification.difficultyReason: Complete products by applying decimal place value and powers of ten across a multiplication grid.

answer.worked:
Each entry is the row heading multiplied by the column heading. Multiplying by $0.001$, $0.01$ and $0.1$ is equivalent to dividing by $1000$, $100$ and $10$, respectively. Multiplying by $1$ leaves the number unchanged. Multiplying by $10$, $100$ and $1000$ moves the decimal point one, two and three places to the right.

For the first row:
$$\begin{align*}0.052\times0.001&=0.052\div1000=0.000052\\0.052\times0.01&=0.052\div100=0.00052\\0.052\times0.1&=0.052\div10=0.0052\\0.052\times1&=0.052\\0.052\times10&=0.52\\0.052\times100&=5.2\\0.052\times1000&=52\end{align*}$$
Each successive row heading is ten times the previous one, so every product directly below another is ten times that product. Apply this to obtain all entries in the completed grid.
